newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria approves oil deal with Hungary's MOL.
newsitem.headline: Syria approves oil deal with Hungary's MOL.

text.p: Syria has approved a contract with the Hungarian oil and gas company Magyar Olj-es Gaizpari (MOL) for exploration and production of oil in Syria, officials said on Wednesday.
They said that Syria's parliament had approved the contract according to which the Hungarian company would spend at least $12 million to explore for oil in an area of 5,000 sq kms.
Oil industry sources said that MOL had 44 months to conduct the first phase of exploration in Palmyra East, some 250 km northeast of Damascus, as well as two extension periods of 24 months each.
A senior MOL official told Reuters his company had great hopes that oil and gas would be discovered in the area, which is close to the main Syrian oilfields that are producing light crude.
"Although the area was explored before by other companies, we have big hopes to find oil because we have better geologists and better experience," the spokesman said.
Oil industry sources say Syria produces over 400,000 barrels of light oil per day (bpd) from the region close to MOL's concession area.
Syria currently produces around 600,000 bpd of heavy and light crude. Over 320,000 bpd is sold on the world market and the rest is for local consumption.

According to an initial geological survey in Syria over 831 structures were identified as areas with possible deposits of oil. Of these, 293 were drilled and oil was found in about 160 structures, oil sources said.
Under the contract MOL would have to drill at least four exploration wells during the first 44 months.

During the extension periods it should drill two wells and spend at least $5.5 million during each period of 24 months. MOL should also conduct a three-dimension survey for about 200 km long, and a two-dimension survey for 700 km, officials said
If oil is discovered in commercial quantities a new company would be formed with equal shares by Syria's Petroleum Company (SPC) and MOL. The contract's period would be 25 years.
The MOL official said his company had experience in the oil industry in Hungary for over 60 years.
It now has projects in several countries including Qatar and Yemen in addition to other joint ventures with several multinational oil companies.
